post_text:
Cleveland: 22% absenteeism in 2019. 18% by 2024.
Memphis: 20% in 2019. 29.6% by 2024.
Same poverty rate. Opposite directions.

The difference wasn't money.

Five cities entered 2020 with nearly identical profiles. All five received comparable ESSER dollars per pupil after COVID. By 2024, Cleveland cut 4 points, Detroit cut 5 points, Memphis added 9.6. The divergence traces to one decision: Cleveland and Detroit deployed school-by-school attendance advocates who contacted families within 3 days of any unexcused absence — before students crossed the 18-day chronic threshold. Memphis ran district-wide awareness campaigns. The research was unambiguous. The data confirmed it.
